extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community: investigators, grant applicants, research administrators, and institutional officials
extracted.subtask_short: NIH extramural news for grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update page summarizing recent NIH policy changes, resources, and guidance affecting grant applications, review, data-sharing, and reproducibility. Useful for investigators and administrators preparing or managing NIH extramural awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. As we continue to encourage approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose models that are scientifically sound and optimally matched to the research question; preference for approaches that increase human relevance and translational potential. Consider NAMs where they are appropriate, but ensure the chosen model aligns with the study objectives and mechanistic/translation goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and award structure
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying to PF5, follow the new application format and be aware that applications can be split into linked awards post-review and before Just-in-Time. Review the NIH video/overview for specific formatting and structural expectations to avoid administrative or structural errors in submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format when preparing DMS Plans; follow the simplified required elements specified by NIH rather than older templates. Ensure the plan addresses required elements in the new format to meet policy and application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations (Gold Standard Science plan & Highlighted Topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science... NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility. In support of this plan, NIH has launched a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should explicitly consider replication and reproducibility in study design, methods, and proposed analyses. NIH may highlight replication/reproducibility as a topic for applications and awards; incorporate practices (e.g., preregistration, robust statistical planning, transparent methods/data sharing) that strengthen reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation: 'Competitive But Not Discussed' in peer review scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: “Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as ‘competitive but not discussed.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that after certain review process modifications, an application can be scored as 'competitive but not discussed' if it falls into the middle third of the study section ranking. This affects applicant expectations for discussion and potential follow-up (e.g., Just-in-Time requests) and indicates that being 'competitive' may not guarantee discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within CSR — implications for review process
rubrics_metrics.description: “In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) ... the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware that peer review processes, assignment, and possibly review criteria/operations are being consolidated under CSR, with stated goals of strengthening efficiency, competition, and transparency. Monitor announcements for changes in review procedures, deadlines, or assignment practices that could affect application preparation and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NIH communications and resources to prepare submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The page repeatedly points to NIH resources (videos, new formats, notices) and encourages subscribing to NIH Extramural Nexus and reviewing posted materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly consult NIH news, guide notices, overview videos, and updated templates (e.g., DMS Plan formats) to ensure applications conform to the latest expectations; subscribe to NIH Extramural Nexus and use NIH-provided materials to avoid outdated formats or misunderstandings about policy changes.
